look_alike_groups.note: Winged ants and winged termites swarm at the same time of year and are often confused. Check the waist (pinched vs. straight), antennae (bent vs. straight), and wing pairs (unequal vs. equal length).
Both have eight legs and startle people the same way. A scorpion has visible pincers and a segmented tail with a stinger; a spider does not.
The brahminy blind snake is small, shiny, and nearly legless-looking — it's very often mistaken for an earthworm.

black-widow.note: v1 did not distinguish black vs. brown widow; maps to the Widow Spiders subgroup rather than over-claiming one species.

honey-bee.note: v1 did not distinguish a resting swarm from an established wall colony (very different next steps); maps to the Bees subgroup. Judgment call — owner should confirm this reads correctly in the app fallback.

mosquito.note: v1 was genus-agnostic; maps to the Mosquitoes group rather than a specific Aedes entry.

sod-webworm.note: v1 aliases covered both sod webworm and armyworm ("Sod Webworms / Armyworms"); maps to the Lawn Caterpillars subgroup, which holds both entries.

flea.note: Only entry today is cat flea; maps to the group so a future dog-flea entry does not orphan this mapping.

tick.note: v1 aliases were tick species names, not mites; maps to the Ticks subgroup.

silverfish.note: The dedicated firebrat entry now resolves that separate species; this legacy slug maps only to silverfish.

millipede.note: The generic v1 label covers multiple catalog species; maps to the Millipedes subgroup.

centipede.note: The v1 entry mixed the qualified house-centipede name with generic centipede labels; maps to the group now that another centipede species is cataloged.

rodent.note: v1 was species-agnostic (rat, mouse, or generic droppings); maps to the Rats & Mice group.

whitefly.note: v1 aliases named both a generic "whitefly" and "ficus whitefly" (a different species added by another owner); maps to the subgroup so it doesn't over-claim species.

aphid-scale.note: v1 combined aphids, scale, mealybugs, and sooty mold into one entry, spanning several subgroups; maps to the Tiny Plant Pests group.

beneficial.note: v1 lumped many unrelated beneficial species (lady beetle, lacewing, dragonfly, mantis, earthworm, anole, gecko, frog, toad) under one slug. No single catalog node covers all of them without over-claiming, so this resolves to null; the caller should keep its own generic beneficial fallback copy until each species is looked up individually.
